**0082 IS BUILT AND READY FOR YOUR REVIEW, ACROSS TWO COMMITS: `169a349` (the build) and `c635e77` (what three other readers found in it).** Review both as one change. hv's ruling: the globbing is kept and documented, one helper holds the rule, a word-less command line is refused naming its key.

**Census.** shfmt's syntax tree over all 43 tracked runtime shell files, control fixture of six known shapes and three negatives first: EIGHT calls take their command word from an unquoted expansion -- lib/resolve 766/783 (an option's `run:`, gated and bare), lib/resolve 885/892 (a command's, gated and exec'd), lib/gatecmd, lib/cmd/check, `commands.fullcycle.restore`, `release.notes.run`. bin/devbin's `eval` of `project.referent` is a different rule, out of scope. **I read your pre-state.md rather than taking your summary of it: your table agrees on all eight config-value sites, and your four extras are correctly out of scope.** All eight now ask `run_words`.

**The helper (lib/helpers).** `run_words <array> <key> <value>`: splits on space, tab and newline whatever the caller's IFS; every word is a glob pattern matched where the caller stands, which each site makes the directory the command runs from; a word matching nothing passes as written; never eval'd; a value with no words is refused naming <key>. It pins `set -f` and the six glob shopts for the split alone and puts them back. `has_words` is the same question without the glob, which is what a validator can answer. `warn_no_words` holds the one refusal sentence both use.

**Arms: 27 new, each seen red first, counted off the commits rather than off memory** (`git show <sha> -- tests/ | grep -c '^+@test'`): 11 runwords.bats, 9 helpers.bats, 2 release.bats, 3 fullcycle.bats, 2 config.bats. No arm deleted. Suites at `c635e77`: helpers 73, runwords 11, release 72, config 60, fullcycle 52, builtins 39, dispatch 78, surfaces 40; syntax and lint 0 breaches over 45 files. Full suite re-running as I send this; I will send the number.

**THE MUTANT CAMPAIGN, INCLUDING ITS SURVIVOR.** 15 mutants in `git archive` exports, each anchor verified to appear exactly once, each run against a fresh copy of a pristine export, tree-diffed before (exactly one file differs) and after the restore (nothing differs).

**Two harness controls first, because a campaign in exports is worthless if the exports read the shared tree's lib:** a pristine export's runwords.bats is 11/11 green, and an export whose `run_words` is overridden to always refuse goes 10 of 11 RED. The second is the one that carries the proof.

Killed, each read at its own arm: globbing off in the helper (9), the refusal removed (7), the IFS pin removed (2), the shopt pin (1), the noglob pin (1), `has_words` on `[[:space:]]` (1), the option site (5), the command site (2), `cfg_has` back to `[ -n ]` (2), gatecmd (1), restore (2), validation branch (1). **Plus the two gated sites your checklist asked for by name and my first pass did not cover: option-gated (2) and command-gated (1).**

**M13, the notes.run RUN site, SURVIVED.** Nothing in the suite killed a bypass of it. The old expansion globbed at the root too, inside the same cd, so the existing glob arm cannot separate the readings -- and the IFS angle is a dead end, since line 936 has pinned IFS locally since before 0082. **The glob state is what separates them.** New arm: the site under `env SHELLOPTS=noglob` with `notes.run: bin/n*tes`, which resolves only if devbin turned globbing back on. Red under the mutant, green with run_words. **The survivor was the most useful result of the campaign and I would not have had it from reading.**

**YOUR FINDING IS IN, AND MY FIRST ARM FOR IT WAS VACUOUS.** The split lands in a local and is copied to the caller after the shopts are restored. I wrote the arm, it went green, I reverted the hardening to prove it red -- **and it stayed green**, because my reversion had moved the failing assignment to before the shopt loop, where there was nothing yet to leak. Faithful reversion puts it back after the loop: `rc=1 nullglob=off dotglob=off`, exactly as you predicted. Also in: the nameref name guard (status 2), your stronger GLOBIGNORE wording, and critic-shell's `notes_select` finding.

**DECLARED LIMITS, FOR YOU TO ATTACK.**
- **`notes_select` has NO arm and will not get one.** There is provably no input separating `has_words` from `run_words` there: the only caller cd's to the root, and with nullglob unset a non-matching word passes through, so the array is non-empty exactly when has_words is true. Contract fix, declared as one. **If you find an input that separates them, I am wrong and it needs an arm.**
- Same shape at lib/cmd/check: no catalogue line holds a glob character or is blank, and bash never imports IFS from the environment. Its bypass mutant is equivalent; the site moved for one rule, not a behaviour.
- A command-line key added to the schema without joining `_cfg_path_command_line` is validated as ordinary text. Nothing catches that but a reader.
- The census is a method, not a test: a ninth site is caught by review. A source arm over bash's own parser was prototyped and dropped -- it missed `exec $run` on macOS, since BSD awk has no `\<`.
- WP-03's materialised root does not exist, so `notes.run`'s "the root it answers for" is checked in the code reaching the expansion after the cd, not driven.

**Reconciliation so you do not lose an hour on it: your board says the `[%s]` case matches a file named `sn` and mine says `s`. Both right, different words.** Your probe's line was `printf [%s]\n *.md`, whose second word is `[%s]\n` -- a one-character class then an escaped literal `n`, so two characters. Mine is `./args [%s] *.md`, so one.

**Also yours, in existing test code rather than in the new work, and already repaired in `c635e77` with a red-first proof:** builtins.bats:662 drove through a helper that cd's to the project root before invoking devbin, so the caller was never anywhere else and the arm's own "not the caller's directory" could not fail.

**What I most want from you:** drive your five pre-state rows against the fix rather than reading my account of them; attack the `notes_select` limit above; and say whether you find a ninth site.
